title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into an environment they were not prepared for: sustained gridlock during a major public event that drained their batteries faster than anticipated. The system had no contingency for heavy, unexpected congestion that kept vehicles stationary for extended periods. What would have caught this is either battery capacity modeling that accounted for worst-case traffic scenarios in dense urban settings, or a human dispatch system that managed vehicle availability and routed them away from high-risk times and locations.

The failure extended to passenger experience: riders sat immobilized in standstill traffic for nearly two hours while vehicles were manually cleared from roads. A secondary hazard also emerged when a vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks in the street, showing that the system's environmental sensing or planning did not account for debris in roadways during public celebrations.

It is not established whether this represents a gap in how Waymo tests its vehicles before deployment, how it manages fleet operations during predictable surge events, or both.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. At least one vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had set off in the street, though no injuries were reported.

Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. Some passengers reported frustration as they sat in standstill traffic for nearly two hours while these vehicles were removed from roadways. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office said they will have conversations with public and private partners to ensure smoother traffic management for future events. This incident follows a December outage when Waymo vehicles became stranded at non-functioning traffic lights during a citywide power failure.
